subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Prove that the area of the triangle formed by the pair of lines ax²+2hxy+by²=0 and lx+my+n=0 is n²√(h²−ab) : |am²−2hlm+bl²|.

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
Find vertex B and write the area

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say where the third vertex is, and how you handle the difference of the two slopes.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. The pair passes through the origin, so the triangle has O as one vertex and the two meeting points with the line as the other two. Split the pair in slope form.
steps.memory_tip: The pair passes through the ORIGIN, so O is one vertex for free. Split the pair in slope form.
lines: On equating like term coeff., we get

recall.must_convey: That the pair is split as (m₁x − y)(m₂x − y) with m₁ + m₂ = −2h/b and m₁m₂ = a/b.
accept: split the pair into two slope form lines and equate coefficients
the sum of the slopes is minus two h over b and the product is a over b
write the pair as m one x minus y into m two x minus y
slopes sum and product teesukovali
match the coefficients

steps.why: Every proof in this chapter starts the same way: SPLIT the pair into its two separate lines with unknown coefficients, then match coefficients against the given equation. That dictionary between (a, h, b) and the two lines is what every later step spends.
common_mistakes: Writing m₁ + m₂ = 2h/b without the minus sign.
Dividing by a instead of b.

steps.label: Draw the pair and the cutting line
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark but worth drawing. Both lines of the pair pass through the ORIGIN, so O is one vertex for free — the picture is what makes that visible, and it is why only two vertices have to be found.
steps.memory_tip: The picture makes it visible that only TWO vertices have to be found.

recall.must_convey: That the two lines through the origin and the cutting line are sketched, forming triangle OAB. Naming the drawing is full credit — it cannot be spoken.
accept: draw the two lines through the origin and the line that cuts them
sketch the triangle O A B formed by the pair and the line
show that both lines of the pair pass through the origin
pair rendu lines origin gundaa vellthaayi, line cut chesthundi
draw the triangle formed by the pair and the line

steps.why: A homogeneous second-degree equation always represents two lines through the ORIGIN, so the third vertex is free — which is what shortens the area formula to ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁|.
common_mistakes: Drawing the pair away from the origin, which a homogeneous equation cannot represent.
Drawing the cutting line through the origin too, which would collapse the triangle.

steps.label: Find vertex A
steps.margin_note: Two marks. One vertex is where the given line meets the first of the two lines — solve that pair by cross-multiplication, keeping everything in letters.
steps.memory_tip: Solve the given line against the first of the pair by cross-multiplication, keeping everything in letters.
lines: By solving lx + my + n = 0 and m₁x − y = 0 we get A

recall.must_convey: That solving the given line with m₁x − y = 0 gives A = (−n/(l+mm₁), −nm₁/(l+mm₁)).
accept: solve the given line with the first line of the pair by cross multiplication
this gives the first vertex A in letters
A is minus n over l plus m m one and so on
modati line tho solve chesthe A vasthundi
find the first vertex

steps.why: The third vertex is the ORIGIN, since both lines of the pair pass through it — so only two vertices need finding, and the area formula for a triangle with a vertex at O is short.
common_mistakes: Solving the given line against itself.
Sign slip in one of the three cross-multiplication denominators.

steps.label: Find vertex B and write the area
steps.margin_note: Two marks. B comes from the same working with m₂ in place of m₁. With O at the origin, the area reduces to ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| — no third coordinate needed.
steps.memory_tip: With O at the origin the area collapses to ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| — no third coordinate needed.
lines: Similarly, we get  B = (−n/(l + mm₂),  −nm₂/(l + mm₂))
The area of the triangle with vertices O(0,0), A(x₁,y₁), B(x₂,y₂) is  Δ = ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁|

recall.must_convey: That B is found the same way and the area is ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| with O at the origin.
accept: B is the same with m two instead of m one
the area with a vertex at the origin is half mod x one y two minus x two y one
substitute both vertices into the area formula
B ni same ga teesukoni area formula vaadali
write the area of the triangle

steps.why: Putting one vertex at the origin removes two of the six terms in the general area determinant, which is why the pair-through-the-origin setting keeps this manageable.
common_mistakes: Using the full three-vertex determinant and mis-expanding it.
Losing the n² when multiplying the two numerators.

steps.label: Convert to a, h, b
steps.margin_note: The last three marks. m₂ − m₁ is not in the dictionary, but (m₁+m₂)² − 4m₁m₂ is — so square the difference first, then substitute (1) and clear the b's.
steps.memory_tip: m₂ − m₁ is not in the dictionary, but (m₁+m₂)² − 4m₁m₂ is — so SQUARE the difference first.
lines: = ½ · n²√((m₁ + m₂)² − 4m₁m₂) / |l² + lm(m₁ + m₂) + m²(m₁m₂)|

recall.must_convey: That (m₂ − m₁)² = (m₁+m₂)² − 4m₁m₂ lets (1) be substituted, giving the stated area.
accept: square the difference of the slopes so the sum and product can be used
m two minus m one is the root of the sum squared minus four times the product
substitute from one and the b denominators cancel
difference of slopes ni sum and product tho rayali
this gives the required area

steps.why: Only the SUM and PRODUCT of the slopes are known, never the slopes themselves — so any expression in them must first be written through those two, which is what the identity does.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that b appears in both numerator and denominator and cancels.

insider_note: Only the SUM and PRODUCT of the slopes are needed, never the slopes themselves: m₁ + m₂ = −2h/b, m₁m₂ = a/b. Write m₂ − m₁ as √((m₁+m₂)² − 4m₁m₂), and the b cancels top and bottom at the end.
